day-88-act-01.title: Retrieval Gauntlet Design: Sealed Task Inventory and Declared Assistance Conditions
day-88-act-01.prerequisites: Days 85-87 capstone integration and the completed Learning Project sequence (autograd, pretraining, real LoRA, evaluable agent, CI delivery).
day-88-act-01.objective: Assemble the fixed, sealed task inventory for unaided retrieval across five domains and declare assistance conditions before any attempt, so independent evidence is never inferred from assisted output.
day-88-act-01.instructions:
1. Understand why this day exists: retrieval practice (the testing effect) produces durable memory better than rereading; today converts the whole curriculum into fixed, unaided checks.
2. The sealed gauntlet covers exactly five domains, each traceable to real evidence days:
   - Domain PY (Core Python): values, control flow, functions, containers, exceptions, files (Days 4-12).
   - Domain GIT (Git & Debugging): branching, diff reading, failure diagnosis, safe recovery on disposable repositories (Days 13-15, 79-81).
   - Domain MATH (Mathematics): derivatives, chain rule, probability, cross-entropy interpretation (Days 16-30).
   - Domain GRAD (Gradients & Autograd): computation graphs, shared-node accumulation, finite-difference verification (Days 31-33 and projects/autograd).
   - Domain MODEL (Model Reasoning): tokenization, causal masking, parameter ledgers, loss/perplexity reading, LoRA accounting, agent-loop behavior (Days 34-87).
3. For each domain, fix three task IDs now — no improvisation mid-check. Map every task to a recovery day in case it is missed.
4. Declare the assistance condition in writing: Independent Mastery Check — no AI, no notes, no browser, ≤105 minutes of the 120-minute block, start time recorded. Declared condition is honest self-report, not claimed surveillance.
5. The agent may help you *organize this inventory only*; it must not author, solve, or grade any sealed task.

day-88-act-01.hint: Use one row per task, e.g. {"domain":"GIT","task_id":"GIT-1","recovery_day":"day-14","declared_condition":"independent"}.

day-88-act-02.title: Independent Check A: Core Python and Git Debugging (AI-Free)
day-88-act-02.prerequisites: Day 88 Activity 1 sealed inventory declared; assistance condition: independent (no AI, no notes).
day-88-act-02.objective: Demonstrate unaided core-Python and Git/debugging competence on fixed tasks: implement a text utility with tests, diagnose a failing test output, and plan safe Git recovery on a disposable repository.
day-88-act-02.instructions:
Task PY-1 (45 min): Implement top_k_words(text, k) — return the k most frequent words of the input, case-insensitive, punctuation stripped, ties broken alphabetically. Write the function and a unittest covering: normal counts, tie order, empty text, k larger than vocabulary.
Task GIT-1 (35 min): On a disposable clone, you committed work directly on main by mistake. Write the exact command sequence that moves the commit onto a new branch fix/login and restores main to the remote state — plus the command that recovers a branch tip you deleted yesterday. Work may be simulated on a scratch repo; destructive flags are permitted only inside the disposable fixture.
Task DBG-1 (25 min): Given this failing output — FAIL: test_parse (KeyError: 'total') and FAIL: test_window (expected 6 items, got 7) — write the two most probable root causes and the first diagnostic command you would run for each.
Record every answer in your worksheet; each claim must be checkable by a command (python -m unittest, git log, git reflog).
day-88-act-02.exercise_prompt: Deliver worksheet entries: PY-1 implementation + test output; GIT-1 command sequence with an explanation of which worktree state each command produces; DBG-1 two diagnoses with diagnostic commands.
day-88-act-02.hint: collections.Counter.most_common does not define alphabetical order for ties — sort explicitly. For GIT-1, `git branch` does not move HEAD; `git reflog` finds lost tips.
day-88-act-02.mastery_criterion: All three tasks answered correctly with runnable verification, entirely unaided.

day-88-act-03.title: Independent Check B: Mathematics, Gradients, and Model Reasoning (AI-Free)
day-88-act-03.objective: Demonstrate unaided quantitative reasoning: a hand-computed chain-rule gradient, a transformer parameter ledger, causal-mask reasoning, LoRA adapter accounting, and loss/perplexity interpretation against recorded artifact values.
day-88-act-03.instructions:
Task M-1 (25 min): For f(a,b) = a*b + a, at a=2.0, b=3.0: compute df/da and df/db by hand (df/da = b + 1 = 4.0, df/db = a = 2.0), then state which finite-difference formula and step h you would use to verify in float64, and why two-sided difference beats one-sided.
Task M-2 (25 min): Recompute the parameter ledger for the pretraining smoke configuration (vocab=65, block=16, n_layer=2, n_head=2, n_embd=16): token_embedding = 65*16 = 1040; position_embedding = 16*16 = 256; attention/layer = 4*(16*16) = 1024; mlp/layer = 2*(16*64) = 2048; total = 1040 + 256 + 2*(1024+2048) = 7440. Compare with projects/pretrain/artifacts/run_artifact.json.
Task M-3 (20 min): In three sentences, explain why attention position t must not read position t+1 and how the upper-triangular causal mask enforces this.
Task M-4 (25 min): For d_model=1024 and LoRA rank r=16 on one projection: adapter parameters = A(16x1024) + B(1024x16) = 32768 versus dense 1024x1024 = 1,048,576 (~3.125%). State where the alpha/r scaling enters.
Task M-5 (25 min): Interpret val_loss 4.0372 from the smoke artifact: perplexity = exp(4.0372) ≈ 56.7. Explain why this is expected for a 10-step CPU smoke run and name two observations that would falsify training health (e.g., rising loss, non-finite gradients).
day-88-act-03.exercise_prompt: Work all five items with formulas and units shown; then check numeric answers against the recorded artifact fields — record agreement or discrepancy honestly.
day-88-act-03.hint: Perplexity = exp(cross-entropy loss). The two-sided difference f'(x) ≈ (f(x+h) − f(x−h))/(2h) has O(h^2) error; use h≈1e-5 for float64.
day-88-act-03.answer:
M-1: df/da = b + 1 = 4.0; df/db = a = 2.0. Verify: (f(2.00001,3) − f(1.99999,3))/(2e-5) ≈ 4.0 ± 1e-6.
M-2: 1040 + 256 + 6144 = 7440 — matches run_artifact.json parameter_ledger.total_parameters.
M-3: Position t reading t+1 would leak future tokens, making the next-token loss trivially solvable and breaking autoregressive generation; the upper-triangular mask sets logits to -inf for all j > t before softmax, zeroing their attention weight.
M-4: 32768 trainable vs 1,048,576 dense (~3.1%); the adapter output is scaled by alpha/r = 32/16 = 2.0 before being added to the frozen base weight's output.
M-5: exp(4.0372) ≈ 56.7 — high but sane for a 10-step CPU smoke run on tinyshakespeare; it verifies plumbing, not convergence. Falsifiers: train loss rising, NaN/Inf gradients, checkpoint reload mismatch.
day-88-act-03.mastery_criterion: All five quantitative items answered correctly with shown work, unaided, and checked against recorded artifact values.

day-88-act-04.title: Assessment: Transparent Rubric Scoring and the Unmet-Criteria Ledger
day-88-act-04.objective: Score every sealed task against a fixed 0/1/2 rubric, compute domain subtotals, and produce the unmet-criteria ledger that routes each miss to a named recovery activity — with the honest-evidence rules stated.
day-88-act-04.instructions:
1. Rubric (fixed before scoring): 0 = absent or incorrect; 1 = partially correct (right method, one arithmetic/logic element wrong, or verification missing); 2 = fully correct and command-verifiable.
2. Domain pass bar: ≥5/6 per domain AND no single task scored 0. Overall pass: all five domains at bar.
3. For every item scored <2, write a ledger row: {task_id, miss_type ∈ {concept_gap, slip, ambiguity, evidence_gap}, recovery_day, next_attempt_date}.
4. Publish score_sheet.json: per-task scores, domain subtotals, pass/fail per domain, and all ledger rows.
5. State the honesty rules aloud in the sheet header: an Independent Mastery Check is evidence of unaided ability; Agent-Assisted results never substitute; this is not an official certification and does not claim universal three-month mastery — unmet criteria stay visibly unmet.
day-88-act-04.exercise_prompt: Emit score_sheet.json with all fields populated and the ledger rows written for every non-perfect item; include the honesty_rules header verbatim.
day-88-act-04.hint: A 1-point miss on PY-1 tie-breaking maps to recovery day-09 (loops/containers); a causal-mask concept gap maps to day-43.
day-88-act-04.mastery_criterion: Produce a complete, honest score sheet and remediation ledger; unmet items remain visibly unmet and every miss carries a named recovery route.
